Q: Text Editor in C++ A:

But the problem is that I can't use containers (such as string, vector, etc. I mean I have to use pointers instead)

Are you sure your project suppose to be in C++? I mean this is strange limitation for a school/learning C++ project.
If you can't use std containers, then you can write your own, to hide fact of using "pointers". You can design API of this classes to be same as equivalent of std, so switching between your own implementations and standard library would be seamless.

Q: WPF ListView items not displaying data from Binding (showing blank or wrong values)" A:

Be sure that your DataContext instance of the ListView is set properly because perhaps you are using something directly from the View Model or perhaps your DataContext should be set to some kind of ancestor. Be sure too that your ItemSource of the control is being set as a ObservableCollection<YourModelClass> and to fix that binding to this ItemSource={Binding MyPeople} . You can find an example with explicit DataContext set if your binding objects are being defined in the View Model.

PS: Try setting an explicit instance of the DataContext of the ListView Control.

Q: Linux C Ncurses issue A:

Actually (there's no sample MCVE to test in this question), ncurses does check for this NULL pointer and is expected to ignore the printw which would be called after the wmove part.

To see this, follow the source-code:

  • mvprintw is always a function call (due to the variable-length argument list)
  • vw_printw is the next step, which calls
  • _nc_printf_string, which sees the null-pointer for the format, and returns null,
  • making vw_printw ignore the call.

Q: Can SQSEvent.Records return multiple values with FIFO SQS and MessageGroupId? A:

why you want to batch process a FIFO queue with the same MessageGroupId? You choose to apply these limitations by having a FIFO in the first place, perhaps you should consider if this should be a standard queue instead.

Note: if we talking about different MessageGroupId, it works concurrently
